title: 1962 AHSME Problem 37
statement: \(ABCD\) is a square with side of unit length. Points \(E\) and \(F\) are taken respectively on sides \(AB\) and \(AD\) so that \(AE=AF\) and the quadrilateral \(CDFE\) has maximum area. In square units this maximum area is:

solutions.text:
Set \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(1,0),\) \(C=(1,1),\) and \(D=(0,1).\) Then \(E=(t,0)\) and \(F=(0,t).\) The shoelace formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} [CDFE]&=\frac{1+t-t^2}{2}\\ &=\frac58-\frac12 \left(t-\frac12\right)^2. \end{aligned} \] Its maximum is \(\frac{5}{8}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(AE=AF=t\) and use coordinates or the shoelace formula
The area becomes \(\frac12(1+t-t^2)\); complete the square
